action: Chapter title card and agenda slide appear; no Blender yet.
why: Opens the chapter.

action: Slides define a blockout as simple shapes for the base forms, with a warning to watch the whole video.
why: Sets the idea that detail is ignored here.

action: Shows four finished example blockouts in the Sculpting workspace, each body part a different flat colour and low-poly.
view: perspective, front-ish, four figures in a row
why: Shows what a blockout looks like: separate coloured parts, no detail.

action: Slide of concept sheets; red marker circles head height versus body on a stylized kid concept.
why: Proportions differ per concept, so read them from the concept.

action: Starts a demo on a finished blockout: picks a torso part and moves it with the grab-move gizmo in Object Mode, front view, in the Sculpting workspace.
why: Prepares to show how fast sculpting goes on a good blockout.

action: With the blockout in place, quickly passes Crease Polish then Clay Strips over the torso to show it already reads well.
why: Shows the payoff of a good blockout.

action: Slide on following the shape language of the concept.
why: Rule 3 of the blockout rules.

action: Red marker over a concept drawing: boxy torso for one body, elongated box limbs for the thin one; then alt-tabs to PureRef, slides and Blender.
why: Shows how to read each body as a few simple solids and keep them through sculpting.

action: Slide lists the first three blockout rules: shape language, parts, simple shapes.
why: Rules 1-3.

action: Opens Add > Mesh and points at Round Cube; shows example figures built only from modified round cubes, each with a Mirror modifier (axis X, Merge 0.001 m) on paired parts.
why: Every part is one round cube reshaped; paired parts use Mirror.
reader_equivalent: mcp round_cube(name) + mirror_x(ob) for paired parts

action: Moves a single new round cube sphere beside the finished figures with the Move gizmo to show every part starts as one; deletes it afterwards.
why: Illustrates one primitive per part and keeps the mesh coarse.

action: Slide adds rule 4 (straight versus curves).
why: Rule 4.

action: Uses the Annotate tool to draw thin blue lines beside a leg in right orthographic, then rotates to perspective views of the torso and legs of a blockout.
why: Draws the straight edge and curved edge on the shin and calf to show straight against curve.

action: Right orthographic view of the whole blockout: a drawn line traces the gentle S, erased afterwards; then front view of the body.
why: Shows the S shape the side silhouette should have.

action: Opens Viewport Shading popover, Lighting MatCap, Object Color Custom, picks black in colour wheel; Specular Lighting off; X-ray bar visible.
why: Turns the body into a flat black silhouette to judge its outline.
reader_equivalent: exec_python: set shading.color_type='SINGLE', single_color=(0,0,0), light='FLAT' on VIEW_3D area; or outline_match

action: Splits the viewport: left small view shows the black silhouette while the large right view stays normal; rotates figure to compare.
why: Keeps the silhouette visible while sculpting.

action: Chapter intro card, then Blender 5.0 splash screen over the default scene with a recent-files list.
why: Starts a new file.

action: In Add > Mesh the Extra Mesh Objects entries (Single Vert, Torus Objects, Math Functions, Gears...) are listed; opens Edit > Preferences, Navigation pane visible.
why: Shows where the Round Cube option comes from and how to enable it.

action: Preferences > Get Extensions, searches 'extra', Extra Mesh Objects listed as installed; then Add > Mesh > Round Cube makes a faceted sphere at the origin.
tool: Get Extensions, Add > Mesh > Round Cube
why: Installs the primitive and adds the first part. Wireframe-faceted look, about 8 quads per cube edge.

action: Right-clicks Round Cube in the Add menu to remove it from Quick Favorites, to show the menu shortcut.
why: Only a convenience for the artist's own menu.

action: Sculpting workspace, sidebar (N) View tab: Focal Length 50 mm edited to 150, Clip Start 0.01 m, End 1000 m; Draw brush active at size 100 px strength 0.5.
why: A long lens makes the view nearly flat so the sculpt does not look distorted.

action: Sphere visibly gets less perspective distortion after the change; closes sidebar with N; splits the viewport.
why: Confirms the longer lens.

action: Sculpt Mode with a small second viewport top-left and the concept images in a corner; the Draw brush is replaced by the Grab brush and its header shows size 432 px, strength 0.400.
why: Grab is the main blockout brush: only broad forms.

action: Brush cursor at 432 px is larger than the whole sphere; X symmetry toggle on in the header; sphere moved around with grab strokes to test.
why: The brush radius is about 1.6 times the part's own radius, so a stroke moves the whole mass smoothly.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_begin(symmetry='X'); grab radius about 0.6 to 0.8 of the part width

action: Grab (size 508 px, strength 0.4) shapes the sphere into an egg seen in perspective; then jumps to front orthographic using the gizmo and hovers the Line Project tool in the toolbar (tooltip: projects onto a plane drawn by a line).
why: Egg-shaped head, then flatten the sides from the front.

action: Side view: Grab at 304 px pulls the lower front forward for the jaw; then Shift+C switches to Crease Polish (size 304 px, strength 0.250) and the cursor circle appears in blue.
why: Jaw forward, then a groove between jaw and skull.

action: Side-on, rear of head: Grab at 252 px pulls the lower back out and up, Shift held for Smooth (F then Shift-drag) smoothing the crown; Alt orbits view.
why: Remove the perfect-ball back of the head.

action: Pulls the back of the head back with Grab (252 to 338 px) in several short drags; F key resizes brush between drags; Ctrl held for inverse.
why: Back of the skull should not be round.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke backward along +Y (0.03-0.05 H) near back skull

action: Shift+T selects Scrape/Fill (size 514, strength 0.700); brushes across the side of the head; back to Grab (424 px) to finish; head ends as a tapered egg.
why: Flatten the side plane then re-form the outline.
reader_equivalent: slice_flat(head, plane just inside the side, mirror_x=True)

action: Ctrl+Tab leaves Sculpt for Object Mode (reference moodboard panel moved aside), then Shift+A opens the Add menu.
why: Prepare to add the neck round cube.

action: Q opens the Quick Favorites menu containing Round Cube and Mirror; picks Round Cube; a new sphere appears at the 3D cursor.
why: Add a new part with one click.

action: Right orthographic, Edit Mode on the new round cube: box selects the lower half in x-ray, E extrudes straight down for roughly one ball diameter, Alt+Z toggles x-ray.
tool: Edit Mode, box select, E extrude
why: Make a capsule for the neck.

action: Right orthographic, Edit Mode, whole capsule selected: G moves it under the skull, S G tweaks, so the top ball sinks into the jaw/back of head; capsule still dead upright and the narrator says not to leave it so.
why: Place the neck inside the head mass.

action: Rotates the capsule in Edit Mode so its lower end swings back (roughly 15 to 20 degrees off upright); Alt+Z repeatedly toggles x-ray to check; the ball top is visible as wire grid inside the head.
why: A neck leans forward as it rises; lower end sits further back.

action: Leaves Edit Mode into Sculpt Mode with Grab 440 px strength 0.400 but the long wall has no edges, so the stroke cannot bend it; returns to Edit Mode with Tab.
why: Shows why loop cuts are needed on the extruded wall.

action: Ctrl+R loop cut: wheel adds several rings along the capsule (preview shows many); Enter confirms and Esc keeps them centred; then back to Sculpt with Ctrl+Tab, Grab 440 px.
why: Give the neck wall geometry to shape.

action: Clicks the X symmetry toggle in the header (X Y Z group top right), then Grab at 440 then ~280-310 px pulls the lower front of the neck out toward the chest; Ctrl+Alt orbits the view.
why: Neck widens at the base to merge with chest.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke from outline_point(neck, z_low, '-Y') outward 0.01-0.03 H

action: Pulls the lower back out toward the upper back, then from user perspective below the chin pulls the lower sides outward (grab ~260-292 px) so they can meet the shoulders; F resizes the brush between strokes.
view: right ortho, then perspective from below
why: Neck base should merge with chest, back and shoulders.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes from outline_point(neck, z, '+Y') and '+X'

action: With Line Project selected (header shows Limit to Segment unchecked) slices the neck bottom flat in right orthographic and perspective; then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode.
why: Trim the neck's lower end flat so the torso can sit on it.

action: Crease Polish at size 122-134 px, strength 0.250, drawn from the jaw corner up to where the ear sits (blue ellipse brush cursor), then Shift-drag smooth around the line.
why: Mark the jaw line that tells where the ear sits.

action: Adds a round cube in Edit Mode; in front orthographic scales it down (S) to about 0.4 of the head's width and moves it (G) to the side of the face; then right orthographic to slide it back to sit behind the jaw line.
why: Place the ear at the side of the head on the jaw line.
reader_equivalent: round_cube('BLK_ears') + place(ear, location=(ear_x, ear_y, ear_z), scale=...)

action: Opens the Symmetry popover in the sculpt header (next to X Y Z toggles) to show the Symmetrize section; Line Project tool active, ear still on one side only.
why: Prepare to mirror the ear to the other side.

action: Symmetry popover shows Mirror X Y Z, Lock, Tiling, Feather on; Symmetrize Direction set to +X to -X, Merge Distance 0.0005; clicks Symmetrize.
why: Copy the +X ear to -X as a second mesh half.
reader_equivalent: mirror_x(ear) (a Mirror modifier does the same)

action: Both ears now present; X symmetry button turned on in the header; Grab (134 then 278 px, strength 0.4) shapes the ear in front orthographic; F x6 resizes brush.
why: Shape both ears at once.

action: Grab 420 px pulls the disc into an ear shape in front view, orbits to the side to see it is a flat disc facing forward, then Tab into Edit Mode to rotate it.
why: The ear should not face straight ahead.

action: Edit Mode on one ear: R then Z rotates about the vertical axis so the front edge turns in and back edge out; G X G Z nudges it into place; back to Sculpt with Ctrl+Tab and Grab 420/268 px.
why: Angle each ear outward.

action: Grab (294-442 px, strength 0.4) pulls the ear into a rounded shape; F x11-x12 resizes the brush; selects the head and Alt+Q to switch the active object to the head and fix its jaw again.
why: Fine-tune the head now that the ear and neck exist.

action: Head objects adjusted with Grab (248-294 px) from perspective/side views (jaw corner and chin) after adding ears and neck; ear now turned outward.
why: After each part, revisit the ones it touches.

action: Final ear tweaks: Grab 126-190 px, strength 0.4, from side perspective, then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode; ears sit on the jaw line at about eye-to-nose level, angled outward.
view: three-quarter back view, then object mode front
why: Done with head, neck and ears; moves to the torso.

action: Object Mode: Q menu > Round Cube adds a new sphere at the origin (named Roundcube.004), roughly the size of the head, ready to become the upper torso.
why: New part for the upper torso.

action: Front orthographic, Edit Mode: G then Z drops the ball straight down below the neck; right orthographic: S then Y scales it flat from front to back, G moves it under the neck.
why: Make the rib cage thinner front to back and place it under the neck.

action: Annotate tool visible, rotates the ball so it tips; then Grab (126 px, 0.400) with Alt orbit starts pulling the neck base into the ball.
why: Tilt the rib cage back and merge the top with the neck.

action: Grab (394 then 248-396 px, F resizing between strokes) pulls the bottom of the ball down and in with the centre front lifted, then side-on pulls the back in; neck base blends into the shoulder line.
why: Rib cage: wide shoulders, tapered bottom.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes starting at outline_point(torso_upper, z, side)

action: Side view, Grab 344-456 px pulls the back inward so it is not rounded; front view broadens the shoulder line; head and neck visible above in the second viewport.
why: Flatten the ball-shaped back.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke on +Y side inward 0.02-0.04 H

action: Starts the middle torso part: a second round cube; X symmetry turned on in the sculpt header; Grab 462 px front view pulling the top into the upper torso.
why: Waist part sits under the rib cage and overlaps.

action: Draws red annotation lines over the character reference (a front photo) to mark the rib cage/waist region and the hips band, then Grab 386-428 px pulls the lower torso ball up into place.
why: Divide the torso into rib cage, waist and pelvis from the reference.

action: Front orthographic: hovers the Line Project tool in the sculpt toolbar (tooltip shows its shortcut) with Limit to Segment unchecked; torso parts stacked as upper and mid ball.
why: Prepare to trim the bottom of the middle torso flat.

action: Grab 262-400 px (F resizing) pushes the middle torso into the rib cage from side and perspective; middle part now blends into the upper part with a visible crease between them.
why: Make the waist overlap the rib cage.

action: Right orthographic Edit Mode: selects the lower ball, R/G to tilt it opposite to the rib cage and place it under the waist; Ctrl+Tab to Object then Edit and back.
why: Pelvis tips forward where the rib cage tips back.

action: Annotate line shows the body centre line; Grab 370 then 328 px (F x4, x9) pulls the pelvis bottom down and the sides out for the hips, X symmetry on.
why: Shape the hips.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes at hips from outline_point(pelvis, z, '+X') moving +X and -Z

action: Grab 428-540 px from the side pulls the back of the pelvis out for the seat; Alt+Q hops between pelvis, mid and upper torso so they all line up from the side.
why: Parts sit on each other like stacked beads, so pull each into the neighbour.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes moving parts' touching ends toward each other

action: Continues side view: pulls the torso's back inward, switches between parts with Alt+Q to blend upper torso back, waist and seat into one S-line.
why: Make the three torso parts read as one flowing trunk.

action: Selects all three torso parts in Edit Mode and scales on X then on Y (S, Y) after comparing with the front and side references; Grab at 412 px next.
why: Widen the whole torso at once to match the reference.

action: Grab at 296-496 px (F x2, x7) refines pelvis bottom and hips; the overall pelvis forms a rounded shape where the legs will start.
why: Pelvis is where the legs come out.

action: Grab at 560 px (large) from far view, then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode and orbits to show torso from side and front before adding the leg part.
view: front and side perspective, whole torso
why: Check the torso is done before legs.

action: Front orthographic Edit Mode: new round cube scaled tall and thin (orange ellipse about 3.5 to 4 times taller than wide), moved with G (Shift for precision) to hang under the pelvis cut on the figure's left.
why: Upper leg, placed under the pelvis.
reader_equivalent: round_cube('BLK_upper_leg'); place(upper_leg, location=(hip_x,0,z), scale=(r_x, r_y, h/2))

action: Add Modifier search typed 'm' selects Mirror; the Mirror modifier panel (Axis X, Bisect off, Clipping off, Merge on 0.001 m) mirrors the leg because it was moved in Edit Mode; R rotates the view.
why: Mirrored legs from one part.

action: Right orthographic Edit Mode: rotates the thigh backward and pulls it into the hips; G Y slides it forward/back; Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode.
why: Keep the body's S curve: thigh tipped back, overlapping pelvis.

action: Alt+Q between pelvis, torso and leg with Grab ~296-392 px (F resizes) so legs, hips and waist flow into each other in front, side and three-quarter views.
why: Parts must work together, not float.

action: New round cube for the lower leg placed under the thigh in front view; adds a Mirror modifier via Add Modifier > search 'm' > Mirror.
why: Lower leg built like the thigh.

action: Grab (410-516 px) makes the lower leg much narrower toward the ankle, then Q opens Quick Favorites in sculpt (Line Project, Lasso Mask, Symmetrize, Relax Slide, Draw Sharp, Mirror, Skin).

settings.Q menu entries: Line Project, Lasso Mask, Symmetrize, Relax Slide, Draw Sharp, Mirror, Skin

why: Narrow the ankle then slice the bottom flat.

action: Front orthographic Grab 394-444 px pulls the lower leg's outer side out and bottom down; a visible step between thigh and shin shows the knee overlap.
why: Shape the shin, narrowing to the ankle.

action: Right orthographic Grab (332-408 px) shapes the lower leg: calf curved at back, shin straighter; Alt+Q hops to the upper leg so the thigh's lower end sits over the shin as the knee.
why: Side profile of the leg: curve behind, straight in front.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes: calf back +Y, shin front kept straight

action: Object Mode then Sculpt on the thigh; Grab 242-328 px shapes the outer hip and thigh from the front perspective; hip line starts to appear.
why: Hips and thighs should flow from the pelvis.

action: Alt+Q cycles through parts with Grab 340-370 px to adjust pelvis, then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode and Q to add a round cube (Quick Favorites list: Origin to Geometry, Round Cube, Purge Unused, Mirror, Solidify...).
why: Adjust before starting the foot.

action: Foot: Front orthographic Edit Mode: new round cube moved to the foot with G and scaled small with S x2; right orthographic scaled down on Z (S Z) into a flat disc under the ankle.
why: The foot is a small flat ellipsoid.

action: Scales the foot on Y to lengthen it, places it under the ankle, Ctrl+Tab to Object, adds Mirror via Q Quick Favorites (tooltip: mirror along local axes over the object origin); both feet appear.
tool: Edit Mode scale (S Y), Mirror modifier
why: Make both feet from one part.

action: Bottom orthographic: Ctrl+Tab via pie menu to Sculpt, Grab 370-404 px pushes each foot from an oval into a rounded rectangle; F resizes brush.
why: Foot outline from below.

action: Right orthographic: Grab 282 px lifts the top back of the foot toward the ankle but drags the sole up with it; undoes with Ctrl+Z, goes to front view to check.
why: Shows why the sole is masked.

action: Hold Shift smooths the foot (F x6 resize), then pulls up the ankle again; right view shows a wedge-shaped foot, front view a wide sole with the ankle narrower.
why: Wedge: tall at the ankle, low at the toe.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab then smooth on BLK_foot

action: Front view Ctrl-drag Lasso Mask on the lower foot, then Alt+M clears the mask; narrator says feet need more refinement; Grab 438 px adjusts toes and ankles from front and perspective.
tool: Lasso Mask (Ctrl+drag), Alt+M clear mask, Grab
why: Hold the sole still while lifting the top back of the foot, then release.

action: Right orthographic Grab 254-462 px shapes the foot as a wedge with heel rounded; Shift smooths the heel; Alt+Q switches to the lower leg to adjust the calf from the side.
why: Side profile: calf curved at back, shin straighter, wedge foot.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes on BLK_foot and BLK_lower_leg from +/-Y

action: Front perspective with legs only: Grab 288-472 px (F resizes, Ctrl+Z x5 undo) refines feet, knees and thighs; the knee shows as a step between thigh bottom and shin top.
why: Check legs against reference from the front.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes on BLK_upper_leg, BLK_lower_leg, BLK_foot

action: Alt+Q hops between thigh and shin with Grab 350-472 px while the narrator tells to compare with the reference; knee overlap region is reshaped.
why: Translate what the reference shows into the sculpt, per part.

action: Orbits Alt-drag between side, three-quarter and front views to check the legs and torso as a whole before starting arms.
why: Proportion check from multiple views before moving on.

action: Opens the sidebar View tab (N) and sets Clip Start from 0.01 m to 0.1; the figure is oversized so near-clipping flickers; focal length shows 150 mm.
why: Hides flicker from the oversized scene (artist notes the scale gets fixed later).

action: Front orthographic Edit Mode: new round cube at the shoulder, lower half selected and extruded down with E into a capsule; A selects all, R rotates it outward, G places it out from the shoulder.
why: Upper arm capsule posed away from the torso.
reader_equivalent: stretch_half(arm, length=4.0, cuts=8); place(arm, rotation_deg=(0,-45,0), pivot=(0,0,0))

action: Object Mode: Shift+D duplicates the upper arm and moves it down the arm for the lower arm; arms form a V pose about 55 degrees from vertical (eyeballed), Mirror modifier panel visible.
why: Lower arm is a copy of the upper arm.

action: Apply Object Transform popup after the Object Mode move; Edit Mode with X-ray (Alt+Z x2): box-selects the far half of the duplicated arm and scales it down (S) so the lower arm tapers toward the wrist.
tool: Apply All Transforms, Edit Mode scale (S)
why: Repair the Object Mode slip, then taper the lower arm.
reader_equivalent: place(arm, location=..., scale=...) keeps transforms at identity

action: G moves the lower arm down; S then Y scales the upper and lower arms down a little each; Alt+Z x-ray on; rotates view to a side perspective to see the arm lined up with the shoulder.
why: Fit arm thickness and position from the side.

action: Front orthographic Edit Mode: Ctrl+R adds another ring on the lower arm, S scales it down, G moves it up; the lower arm begins to show taper curve from elbow to wrist; Ctrl+Z x2 undo.
why: Shape the forearm ring by ring: widest below elbow, narrow at the wrist.
reader_equivalent: stretch_half(lower_arm, length=..., cuts=3) and place per ring

action: Ctrl+R cut count shown in the header while inserting (Cuts: 3, then more); wireframe visible along the lower arm after cuts; Ctrl held while picking rings.
why: Give the forearm enough edges for Grab.

action: Three Ctrl+R cuts typed as 3, Esc; again three cuts in the next stretch and the next; header read 'Cuts: [3]'; then Sculpt Mode, Grab (276 px) and Shift smooth soften the forearm and elbow.
tool: Loop Cut and Slide, Grab, Smooth
why: Forearm is tapered: widest below the elbow, narrowest at the wrist.

action: Upper arm in Edit Mode: Ctrl+R then typing 6 then 8 sets the number of cuts (header shows 'Cuts: 8' final); the capsule shows eight rings along its length.
why: Eight rings let the upper arm bend and carry a bump.

action: Sculpt Mode: Grab (344-422 px, F resizing) pulls the upper arm's lower end up and blends it into the lower arm; Alt+Q switches between arm parts.
why: Make the elbow flow between the two arm parts.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes at elbow ends toward each other

action: Grab (258-342 px) pulls lower arm end up into the elbow and the upper arm down from the side; second Alt+Q to the lower arm checks the forms.
view: side perspective, zoomed out and in
why: Confirm arm forms before adding the front bump.

action: Grab (226-420 px, Alt+Q to hop) pulls the upper arm's lower end into the lower arm; draws a V-shaped bulge ending toward the elbow on the biceps; Annotate pencil checks the line.
why: Biceps ends in a V pointing at the elbow.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes on BLK_upper_arm front face, last point toward elbow

action: Q opens Quick Favorites in sculpt, picks Line Project (tooltip: project the geometry onto a plane defined by a line) and slices one side of the lower arm flat; viewing the leg for comparison.
why: One flat side on the lower arm gives straight-against-curve.

action: Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode, then Edit Mode: A selects all of the arm and S scales it down because it looks too big; the narrator compares against the reference.
why: Resize arm parts together after judging from the reference.

action: Selects the wrist end of the lower arm and scales/moves it to lengthen the forearm; Ctrl+R + Esc adds a cut; Grab (494-520 px) smooths the taper with the V visible on the upper arm.
tool: Edit Mode move, Loop Cut, Grab
why: Lengthen the lower arm and keep the taper.

action: Edit Mode on both arm parts: A, R then G with Shift to rotate and place the arm so it joins the shoulder and sits at the elbow bend; arms form an A-pose shape.
why: Final placement of the arm.
reader_equivalent: place(lower_arm, rotation_deg=(0,0,bend)) with pivot at elbow

action: Add a round cube for the shoulder: Q menu Round Cube appears at the head; in Edit Mode G moves it to the arm joint; the shoulder ball sits on top of the upper arm just outside the torso.
tool: Q Round Cube, Edit Mode move
why: Shoulder part hides the gap between torso and arm.

action: Quick Favorites in Object and in Edit Mode both show Mirror; shoulder ball selected, mirror added through Q > Mirror, the other shoulder appears.
why: Paired shoulder from one part.

action: Grab (366-454 px; F x3, x7 resizing) pulls the shoulder ball outward and down over the top of the upper arm so it flows into it; Annotate line marks the shoulder curve on the front view.
why: Shoulder blends from the neck line into the arm.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes on BLK_shoulder outline_point(... '+X') down and out

action: Grab (292-338 px) from front, then side view, pulls the shoulder ball back so it flows into the back of the torso instead of poking out; Annotate pencil sketches the intended curve.
why: Shoulders must flow into the back, not sit like a ball.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke on BLK_shoulder toward +Y and down

action: Shift+T selects Scrape/Fill (size 302-344 px, strength 0.700, direction Add); sweeps the front of the shoulder ball flat so it is no longer rounded; Grab (310 px) first.
why: Flatten the front face of the shoulder.
reader_equivalent: slice_flat(shoulder, point=..., normal=(0,-1,0)) just inside the surface

action: Shift+C brings Crease Polish (size 100-112 px, strength 0.250); draws the centre line of the back down the torso parts, back view, Alt+Q hops between torso parts.
why: Mark the spine line across the three torso parts.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes brush='crease' snap strength 0.25 radius ~0.02, along x=0 on +Y side

action: Grab (378-444 px; Ctrl+Alt orbit) adjusts legs and the lower arm from the front; narrator says hands will only be a simple shape; Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode, new round cube picked for the hand.
why: Last check of arms and legs before the hand.

action: Hand: Line Project (Limit to Segment off) slices a flat cut on the new round cube, Edit Mode scales it up slightly, then R rotates it to follow the forearm line.
why: Hand continues the line of the forearm.

action: Hand: scaled thin (disc), G moved with Shift to the wrist, shown from the side; rotated to align with the wrist; Ctrl+Tab to Object mode shows an oversized flat disc as the first hand shape.
why: Starts the hand as a simple flat shape.

action: Inflate/Deflate brush chosen from the brush search (size 410 px, strength 0.500, direction Inflate), used on the hand edges; Grab 410 px pulls the hand into shape beforehand.
why: Fatten the two long edges of the palm.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes brush='inflate' (snap) at hand edge, radius ~0.3x hand size

action: Grab (470 px) pulls the hand into the lower arm; Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode shows the full figure with a small mitten hand at the wrist; Q menu mirrors the hand.
why: Mirror the hand to the other side.

action: Deletes a stray object, then looks at the figure and the reference side by side in two panels, orbiting only with Shift+Alt; no edits yet, compares arms, legs and shoulders to the board.
why: Start of the proportion pass: translate the reference onto the sculpt.

action: Rotates the whole figure a few degrees between frames and compares the leg length and arm length with the reference; narrator says the proportions may not be exactly right yet.
why: Judge the whole figure by eye against the board.

action: Grab (376-490 px, F resizing, Alt+Q hopping) pulls the hips out and the shoulders up and out in perspective, front view; works across torso, pelvis and shoulder parts.
why: Adjust shoulder and hip widths after seeing the whole body.
reader_equivalent: scale_parts / grab strokes on shoulders, pelvis

action: Edit Mode on the hand: scales (S) and rotates (R, G) it to fit the wrist after shrinking the arm; Ctrl+Tab via the pie menu between Object, Edit and Sculpt; Grab (394 px) fixes the hand edge.
tool: Edit Mode scale/rotate, Grab, mode pie (Ctrl+Tab)
why: Resize the hand to match the wrist and arm.

action: Grab (296 px) and Crease Polish (116-218 px, strength 0.250) shape the pelvis seat and back centre line; side view shows the arm and hand hanging in the side-view silhouette.
why: Final shaping of the back line and seat.
reader_equivalent: crease stroke snap along x=0 on pelvis back

action: Alt+Q, F, G between parts with Grab (282-374 px) in back view to blend shoulders, waist and seat; Ctrl+Alt orbit to a full figure view.
why: Check from the back: no beads, flowing form.

action: Ctrl+Alt/Alt views then Save As dialog: Blender file browser with a Desktop path and file name field 'Untitled.blend'; save before moving to the next chapter.
why: Keep the parts blockout as its own file.

action: Closing card asks for a review, then the academy logo; chapter ends and the next chapter on the face starts.
why: End of the blockout chapter.
